stack.title: Compose stack
stack.description: {{count}} services deployed from one compose file, reconciled one by one in dependency order.
stack.loadFailed: Could not load the stack status: {{message}}

rollback.title: Roll back the stack
rollback.description: Re-applies an earlier compose file through the normal deploy path and records it as a new revision. Generated passwords stay the same, so data in volumes keeps working.
rollback.none: There is no earlier revision to roll back to yet.

down.title: Tear down {{app}}
down.description: Removes every service and its containers. Named volumes are kept unless you also remove them, so a later deploy under the same name finds its data again.
down.removeVolumes: Also delete the stack's volumes (the data is gone for good)

preview.title: What will deploy
preview.profilesAvailable: Profiles in this file: {{profiles}}. Pass them on the CLI with --profile-name to include those services.
preview.needsRoot: This file bind-mounts host directories, which needs the root ability.
preview.build: build from source (not supported here, use a git deploy)

install.title: Install
install.description: Fill in the settings this template asks for. Generated values are created once, stored encrypted, and reused on every redeploy.
install.namePlaceholder: Leave empty to pick one for you
install.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Prefixes every container and volume of this stack.
install.domainHint: Optional. Point its DNS at this server and HTTPS is set up for you.

publishedPortError.published_port_invalid: Use HOST:CONTAINER with an optional /udp, for example 51820:51820/udp. Each host port and protocol can appear once.
publishedPortError.published_port_conflict: Another service already publishes that host port and protocol. Pick a free host port, or stop the other service.
publishedPortError.published_port_remote_node: Host ports can only be published on the control plane's own node. Move the service to this node or drop the host port.
